method: Compare user outcomes across all groups, asking whether one outcome can work while another fails. Shared screenshots, source modules or controls alone do not establish a duplicate. Preserve distinct wallet types, security requirements, lifecycle stages and interoperability checks.

merges.intent: Export a watch-only copy of a wallet for monitoring without spending access.
merges.reason: File creation and exclusion of private spending keys are checks for the same export outcome.

merges.intent: Conceal wallet balances and recent activity.
merges.reason: Privacy concealment is counted under Privacy Mode.
Wallet switching is counted once under wallet management.

merges.intent: Inspect transactions in external block explorers.
merges.reason: Explorer handoff is counted once; choosing the service remains F23.S08.

merges.intent: Choose which coins fund a transaction, individually or in groups.
merges.reason: Individual and group selection are variants of selecting funding coins.

merges.intent: Keep the node running while the main window is hidden, minimized, or closed, where supported.
merges.reason: Visibility changes must leave the node running. Desktop variants remain part of the evidence scope.

merges.intent: Quit the application and shut down the node cleanly.
merges.reason: Tray or Dock Quit is a shutdown path, with the same clean-exit outcome.

merges.intent: Increase the fee of an eligible transaction by signing and submitting a replacement.
merges.reason: Submitting the replacement completes the fee increase; cost review and unsigned export remain separate.

merges.intent: Handle Bitcoin payment requests transferred from other applications, including while the application is already running.
merges.reason: Import, paste and drag-and-drop are supported handoff paths. Automatic OS forwarding remains an explicit implementation difference.

merges.intent: Verify a receiving address on a compatible signing device.
merges.reason: Receiving-address generation remains under Receive; this criterion now covers device verification alone.

merges.intent: Assess synchronization progress, how far the node is behind, and the estimated remaining work.
merges.reason: Processing rate and remaining-time behavior are verification details of synchronization status; wallet freshness remains F07.S04.

merges.intent: Run advanced node and wallet commands.
merges.reason: Descriptor import, multisig setup, rescans and PSBT combination remain explicit functional scenarios for the console.

merges.intent: Choose an estimated fee based on the desired confirmation speed and understand its expected timing.
merges.reason: Confirmation timing is part of choosing an estimated fee; custom rates and unavailable estimates remain separate.

merges.intent: Receive payment notifications that identify the transaction, wallet, amount, and recipient.
merges.reason: The contents of a payment notification are checks on that notification outcome.

merges.intent: Copy a partially signed PSBT to the clipboard or save it to a file for further signing.
merges.reason: Local and external-signer results are cases of the same partial-PSBT handoff. Collecting additional signatures remains F14.S05.

findings.title: Export a watch-only copy
findings.reason: Creating a watch-only copy and writing that copy to a file describe one export outcome.
findings.recommendation: Combined as F05.S01. File creation and absence of private spending keys are verification steps; cross-node use remains F05.S03.
findings.resolution: Combined file export and creation of the watch-only copy.

findings.title: Watch-only key separation
findings.reason: A copy without spending access already requires spending keys to remain separate. S04 repeats a defining property of S01.
findings.recommendation: Fold S04 into the merged S01 and retain the public-descriptor/private-key assertions as its security checks.
findings.resolution: Added key separation to the same export outcome and retained its security evidence.

findings.title: Conceal balances and activity
findings.reason: Both criteria ask privacy mode to conceal balances and recent activity. Their placement in different groups adds no user outcome.
findings.recommendation: Keep F32.S01 as the counted criterion and cross-reference it from Wallet Overview.
findings.resolution: Concealment is counted under Privacy Mode and linked from Wallet Overview.

findings.title: Switch the active wallet
findings.reason: Choosing which wallet to use and switching between available wallets are the same user action.
findings.recommendation: Keep F02.S03 and cross-reference it from Navigation.
findings.resolution: Wallet switching is counted under wallet management and linked from Navigation.

findings.title: Open a transaction in an external explorer
findings.reason: Both criteria open transaction information in an external block explorer.
findings.recommendation: Keep F16.S09 and reference it from Desktop Integration. Keep configuration of the explorer service, F23.S08, separate.
findings.resolution: Explorer handoff is counted under transaction history and linked from Desktop Integration.

findings.title: Select transaction funding coins
findings.reason: Selecting individual coins or groups is already a way of choosing which coins fund a transaction.
findings.recommendation: Combine as choosing the funding coins individually or in groups. Keep coin inspection, locking and custom change separate.
findings.resolution: Individual and group selection are combined in the funding-coins criterion.

findings.title: Keep the node running while the window is hidden
findings.reason: Both require visibility changes to leave the node running. Minimize, close-to-tray and restore are scenarios for the same outcome.
findings.recommendation: Keep F26.S03, retain supported desktop variants in its test matrix, and link from the tray group.
findings.resolution: Visibility changes that preserve the node are counted under application windows; desktop limits remain visible.

findings.title: Quit cleanly
findings.reason: A tray/dock Quit entry is an activation path for orderly application and node shutdown.
findings.recommendation: Keep F27.S05, with tray/dock Quit as a test path. Keep startup cancellation and Windows session shutdown as distinct cases.
findings.resolution: Tray/Dock Quit is retained as a clean-shutdown test path.

findings.title: Submit a fee increase
findings.reason: Signing and submitting the replacement completes the fee increase described by S01. Neither wording establishes a separate user objective.
findings.recommendation: Combine into increasing the fee of an eligible transaction and submitting its replacement. Retain cost review and unsigned fee-bump export separately.
findings.resolution: Fee increase and signed replacement submission are one outcome.

findings.title: Receive payment links from other applications
findings.reason: Both provide desktop handoff of Bitcoin payment requests into the application. Running-instance delivery and drag-and-drop are supported variants.
findings.recommendation: Keep one handoff criterion under Open Payment URI, preserving both startup/running-instance and drag-and-drop checks.
findings.resolution: Desktop payment-request handoff is counted under Open Payment URI, retaining delivery variants.

findings.title: Receiving-address verification on a device
findings.reason: F08.S08 repeats the verification part of F15.S03, which also includes generating addresses.
findings.recommendation: Give device verification one criterion under External Signer; keep address generation under Receive and reference that coverage.
findings.resolution: Device verification is assessed alone under External Signer; receiving-address generation remains under Receive.

findings.title: Wallet encryption and lock status
findings.reason: Encryption and lock status are repeated; F29.S04 additionally covers key-generation status.
findings.recommendation: Keep encryption/lock status under F06 and narrow F29.S04 to key-generation status, with a link to F06.
findings.resolution: Encryption/lock status stays under F06; F29.S04 now covers only key-generation status.

findings.title: Amount display units
findings.reason: Choosing the displayed denomination is contained in F23.S06 along with language selection.
findings.recommendation: Keep units in one place and narrow the other criterion to language. Preserve both as separately assessable outcomes.
findings.resolution: Language selection and amount-unit selection are separate, single-owner criteria.

findings.title: Synchronization status and wallet freshness
findings.reason: Synchronization progress is repeated in three criteria. Processing rate, remaining work and stale wallet information add distinct conditions.
findings.recommendation: Define one synchronization-status criterion with rate/remaining-work checks and a separate wallet-freshness warning criterion. Replace the other occurrences with references.
findings.resolution: Synchronization status and estimates are consolidated; wallet-freshness warnings remain separate.

findings.title: Advanced RPC commands and examples
findings.reason: S09 lists command examples within S05, including descriptor import, multisig setup, rescan and PSBT combination.
findings.recommendation: Keep command execution as the capability and retain the examples as functional test cases. Keep wallet selection and rescan recovery outcomes independently visible.
findings.resolution: Advanced commands are one console capability with explicit workflow test cases; wallet context and rescan recovery remain distinct.

findings.title: Startup and window preferences
findings.reason: The general startup/window preference row overlaps named outcomes for login startup, minimized startup, background operation and tray visibility.
findings.recommendation: Replace the broad preference row with references to the specific outcomes so each requirement can be accepted separately.
findings.resolution: Removed the broad preference row and linked the four specific startup/window outcomes.

findings.title: Quick access to common tasks
findings.reason: Tray access and general quick-access wording repeat navigation to payments, records and diagnostics. The tray location alone does not add a user goal.
findings.recommendation: Use the concrete navigation outcomes and keep keyboard access separate. Remove broad quick-access rows or turn them into group descriptions.
findings.resolution: Removed generic quick-access rows; concrete task navigation and keyboard access remain explicit.

findings.title: Fee estimate and confirmation timing
findings.reason: Confirmation timing is both an input to fee selection and information the user can assess. The current short wording does not clearly distinguish them.
findings.recommendation: Either combine them or narrow S03 to showing the estimated timing for the chosen fee, including a custom rate; retain that only if it is an independent requirement.
findings.resolution: Expected timing is part of choosing an estimated fee; no separate custom-fee timing capability was introduced.

findings.title: Payment-notification contents
findings.reason: S02 specifies the identifying information inside the payment notifications of S01.
findings.recommendation: Fold transaction/wallet/amount context into the acceptance checks for payment notifications. Keep notification fallback and flood prevention separate.
findings.resolution: Transaction, wallet, amount and recipient context are part of the payment-notification criterion.

findings.title: Wallet and network identity
findings.reason: Network identification is repeated, but F26.S05 also identifies the active wallet and F31.S02 calls out multiple instances.
findings.recommendation: Separate active-wallet identity from active-network identity, with multiple instances as a network-identity scenario.
findings.resolution: Wallet identity and network identity now have separate criteria; multiple instances are a network-identity test case.

findings.title: Device authorization and payment signing
findings.reason: The external-signer part of Send repeats authorization on the signing device. Local signing is a separate part of F09.S07.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the Send criterion to local-key signing and reference device authorization under External Signer, retaining physical-device proof requirements.
findings.resolution: Send covers local-key signing; physical-device authorization remains under External Signer.

findings.title: Continue an incomplete signing workflow
findings.reason: Both preserve an incompletely signed transaction for further signing; F15.S05 is the external-device variant.
findings.recommendation: Use one partial-PSBT handoff criterion with local and external-signer cases. Keep actually combining additional signatures (F14.S05) distinct; successful export alone does not prove it.
findings.resolution: Incomplete-PSBT handoff is consolidated with local and device cases; actually collecting additional signatures remains distinct.

findings.title: Watch-only export versus cross-node recovery
findings.reason: Producing a file does not establish that another node can restore it and monitor the same funds.
findings.recommendation: Keep cross-node interoperability independently checked.
findings.resolution: Keep cross-node interoperability independently checked.

findings.title: Encrypted creation versus encrypting an existing wallet
findings.reason: Protecting an existing wallet can fail independently of creating an encrypted wallet.
findings.recommendation: Keep both lifecycle outcomes.
findings.resolution: Keep both lifecycle outcomes.

findings.title: Multiple wallets versus selecting a wallet
findings.reason: Keeping wallets loaded, choosing the wallet for normal activity, and targeting an RPC command have different state and failure conditions.
findings.recommendation: Keep concurrency, active-wallet selection and RPC execution context separate.
findings.resolution: Keep concurrency, active-wallet selection and RPC execution context separate.

findings.title: No open wallet versus disabled wallet functionality
findings.reason: A node with no open wallet still has wallet functionality available. A wallet-disabled run must retain node controls and application behavior without that subsystem.
findings.recommendation: Keep the disabled-mode acceptance cases; shared screenshots are not enough to merge them.
findings.resolution: Keep the disabled-mode acceptance cases; shared screenshots are not enough to merge them.

findings.title: Unsigned export versus partial signing and signature collection
findings.reason: Preparing a payment, choosing supported wallet/signature types, exporting unsigned data, preserving existing signatures and collecting additional signatures are independently fallible outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Keep their contract boundaries. Use cross-references for shared payment-entry controls instead of treating a common PSBT screenshot as duplicate proof.
findings.resolution: Keep their contract boundaries. Use cross-references for shared payment-entry controls instead of treating a common PSBT screenshot as duplicate proof.

findings.title: Copying data versus saving or sharing images
findings.reason: Generating a request, copying its text, exporting its QR image and sharing it are different usable capabilities. Clipboard copies of addresses or signatures involve different data contracts.
findings.recommendation: Keep copying as a capability, as requested. Do not create extra criteria for the location of a Copy button.
findings.resolution: Keep copying as a capability, as requested. Do not create extra criteria for the location of a Copy button.

findings.title: Progress and recovery stages
findings.reason: Initial application startup, chain download, shutdown and wallet rescans operate at different lifecycle stages. Reporting progress, remaining usable and cancellation can fail independently.
findings.recommendation: Keep stage-specific outcomes. Treat the broad long-running-operation row as a scoped summary, not proof of every operation.
findings.resolution: Keep stage-specific outcomes. Treat the broad long-running-operation row as a scoped summary, not proof of every operation.

findings.title: Explorer settings versus opening a transaction
findings.reason: Selecting an explorer service does not prove that a transaction is handed off using the correct ID.
findings.recommendation: Keep configuration and actual explorer handoff separate.
findings.resolution: Keep configuration and actual explorer handoff separate.

groups.conclusion: Creation variants, naming and existing-wallet encryption have distinct lifecycle contracts.
Wallet switching repeats Navigation; keeping wallets open and targeting RPC are different.
Backup creation, restoration, naming and legacy recovery remain distinguishable.
Format conversion, preserving the original, retaining contents and reopening are separate migration checks.
Apply the requested export merge; key separation is another merge candidate; cross-node recovery remains distinct.
Encryption/lock status overlaps Application Status; key access and relocking remain separate.
Privacy concealment repeats Privacy Mode; wallet freshness participates in the synchronization overlap.
Device verification overlaps External Signer; request generation, copying and sharing remain separate capabilities.
Device signing overlaps External Signer; recipient entry, labeling, amount, validation and watch-only preparation remain distinct.
Desktop payment-link handoff repeats Desktop Integration; parsing a request and receiving it are separate checks.
Estimated confirmation timing needs a clearer boundary from fee selection; custom rates and unavailable estimates remain distinct.
Individual/group selection is part of selecting funding coins; inspection, locks and change handling remain distinct.
Preparation, supported wallet types and unsigned transfer have distinct contracts despite sharing one workflow.
Partial-PSBT handoff overlaps the device variant; import, review, signing, combining and broadcasting remain separately fallible.
Device address verification, payment authorization and partial handoff overlap other groups; device connection and key custody remain explicit.
External explorer handoff repeats Desktop Integration. History browsing, filtering, details, editing, clipboard and CSV are separate outcomes.
Submitting the signed replacement completes fee bumping; reviewing cost, exporting unsigned data and abandoning are distinct.
Record management, receive labels, search, clipboard and CSV remain distinct; labels in payment/history workflows have different contexts.
Signing, verification and copying the signature remain distinct.
Synchronization status repeats status/progress groups; no-open-wallet operation differs from disabled wallet functionality.
Network controls, proxy/router behavior, peer inspection, encrypted transport, bans and copying remain distinct.
RPC workflow examples overlap generic command execution; wallet context, console affordances, logs and traffic remain distinct.
Language/units and startup/window umbrella rows overlap specific groups; configuration precedence and reset recovery remain distinct.
Visibility, quick actions and Quit overlap windows/navigation/lifecycle groups; tray availability and preference remain explicit.
Payment-notification contents belong with their notification outcome; fallback, severity channels and flood suppression remain distinct.
Background operation repeats tray wording; network identity overlaps Desktop Integration; geometry and concurrent diagnostics remain distinct.
Clean shutdown repeats tray Quit; startup modes, startup cancellation, settings recovery and session shutdown have distinct contracts.
Wallet switching is repeated; broad quick access overlaps concrete navigation; keyboard access remains independently useful.
Sync/freshness, wallet lock status and amount units overlap other groups; connection/proxy status and contextual guidance remain distinct.
Synchronization estimates overlap setup/status criteria; operation results, confirmation, diagnostic detail, attention and responsiveness differ.
Payment handoff and explorers are repeated; instance identity overlaps windows; appearance, throttling and help remain distinct.
Balance/activity concealment repeats Overview; history restriction, multiwallet scope and persistence are distinct.
Disabled-wallet mode is different from merely closing wallets; retain node controls and desktop/preferences checks for this mode.
Rediscovery, progress reporting and cancellation are distinct rescan outcomes.

implementation.reason: Receiving-address verification on the signing device is absent; address generation is assessed under F08.S01.

qml.detail: Receiving addresses cannot be verified on a signing device. Address generation is reviewed separately under Receive.

checks: Confirm the generated address on a compatible physical signer.

implementation.reason: Key-generation status is not displayed. Encryption and lock status are assessed separately under F06.S05.

qml.detail: No key-generation status is displayed in the QML interface. Earlier encryption evidence applies to F06.S05.
The display-settings functional test verifies that the selected language persists after restart. Amount-unit selection is assessed under F29.S05.

F29.S05.intent: Choose the denomination used to display amounts: BTC, mBTC, bits, or satoshis.

checks: Observe real peer synchronization and compare the displayed progress with the node’s chain state.
Check the remaining-time estimate after it settles and when throughput changes; a separate processing-rate number is an implementation difference.
Run descriptor import, multisig setup, wallet rescanning and PSBT combination through the console, checking the resulting state.

F28.S03.intent: Access address records, message signing and verification, application settings, and node diagnostics.

qml.detail: The recorded desktop scenario opens address records and node diagnostics, while signing and verification scenarios open their forms. A targeted navigation scenario covering all named tasks has not yet been recorded.

checks: Reach each named task through the application and confirm it is usable. Shortcut location is not an additional criterion.

qml.detail: The wallet-switching check verifies the active wallet and its settings; its capture shows the selected wallet name. The earlier node-only capture supports network identity under F31.S02.

F31.S02.intent: Identify the active Bitcoin network and distinguish instances using different networks.

qml.detail: The existing capture identifies regtest. Other network identities and simultaneous instances still need targeted runtime proof.

checks: Run profiles for the supported Bitcoin networks and distinguish simultaneously open instances.

F09.S07.intent: Sign payments with local spending keys.

qml.detail: Recorded local-wallet payment tests exercise signing and broadcast, including encrypted-wallet authorization and relocking. Physical-device approval is assessed separately under F15.S04.

checks: Authorize a payment with local spending keys and verify the broadcast transaction; include an encrypted wallet.
Export an incomplete result from local and external-signing workflows, verify that existing signatures and outputs are preserved, and resume signing elsewhere.
